common_name: Petite Plum Butterfly Bush (Compact Reddish-Purple Dwarf Buddleja)

planting.note: Set out container plants in spring once soil has warmed; cut the whole plant back hard to 6-12 inches each late winter to keep it compact and encourage the heaviest bloom on new wood.

directions: This naturally dwarf sport of the Nanho strain stays noticeably tighter and rounder than standard butterfly bush, making it a better fit for foundation plantings and small gardens. Slender gray-green leaves set off dense, slightly arching panicles of reddish-purple flowers that open from midsummer into fall. Give it full sun and well-drained soil; it tolerates heat and drought once established and draws butterflies steadily through the season. Hard annual pruning in late winter keeps the habit dense rather than leggy.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Versicolor Hardy Fuchsia (Variegated Cream-and-Pink Foliage Fuchsia)

planting.note: Plant out after the last frost once the soil has warmed; in colder zones mulch the crown heavily for winter and treat top growth as die-back perennial.

directions: Grown as much for its foliage as its flowers, this selection carries small gray-green leaves irregularly edged in cream with a pink flush on new growth, set against an upright, bushy framework of slender red stems. Small pendant flowers with red tubes and sepals and a violet-purple corolla appear from midsummer onward and draw hummingbirds reliably. Part shade keeps the variegation brightest and prevents leaf scorch, while any reverted all-green shoots should be cut back promptly to keep the plant from reverting entirely. Where winters are too cold for the top growth to persist, it regrows readily from the root each spring in a sheltered, well-mulched spot.
sources: RHS Award of Garden Merit plant profile
